description:
SAC is a standard interface for CSS parsers, intended to work with CSS1, CSS2, CSS3 and other CSS derived languages.  

Security Fix(es):  

  * libreoffice: heap buffer overflow in PDF import stream handling (CVE-2026-63274)
  * libreoffice: stack buffer overflow in CFF to Type 1 font conversion (CVE-2026-63276)
  * libreoffice: stack buffer overflow in CFF font hint handling (CVE-2026-63275)
  * libreoffice: libreoffice: Arbitrary code execution via remote Java database driver (CVE-2026-63277)


Bug Fix(es) and Enhancement(s):  

  * [libbase] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275415)
  * [flute] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275416)
  * [libserializer] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275417)
  * [libloader] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275418)
  * [libformula] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275419)
  * [librepository] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275420)
  * [libfonts] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275421)
  * [liblayout] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275422)
  * [pentaho-libxml] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275423)
  * [pentaho-reporting-flow-engine] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-275424)
  * [sac] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-277813)
  * [libreoffice] LibreOffice packages using EOL Java (after November 2026) (JIRA:AlmaLinux-260518)
  * [AlmaLinux 8.10] Base Report Wizard fails with packaged Pentaho reporting engine (JIRA:AlmaLinux-286491)


For more details about the security issue(s), including the impact, a CVSS score, acknowledgments, and other related information, refer to the CVE page(s) listed in the References section.
